semantics: procedural transport (master brief §34/§35/§36) + the §33 structural-innovation measurement over standalone .vole streams. src/transport.rs frames a standalone stream into packets [len:u32][kind:u8][seq:u64][body] (13 B/packet overhead) in the canonical emission order HEADER OBJECT* PALETTE* CHECKPOINT INTERVAL* INTEGRITY. Packet payloads are generated by the shared format::*_bytes record helpers, so every body is byte-identical to the standalone writer's record; the Receiver rebuilds the canonical prefix and plays it through the normative parser (decoder::decode_bytes + materialize_all) - no transport-side state machine duplicates the materializer. Loss is a typed VoleError::TransportGap; recovery retransmits from the gap (Transmitter::encode_from(seq)); a receiver that fell behind rolls back to the checkpoint (Receiver::reset_to_checkpoint) and replays forward, replay bounded by the v1 Limits envelope (max_transition_replay / max_checkpoint_distance) exactly as standalone decode. Integrity is the standalone stream's own BLAKE3 trailer semantics (Receiver::verify / reassemble). Store-backed streams (external object declarations, Phase P) are deliberately not standalone and transport rejects them (recorded boundary).

courts.packetize_reassembles_byte_exact: source 1098 B -> 30 packets (24 interval, 2 object, 1 palette, 1 checkpoint, 1 header, 1 integrity) -> framed 1488 B; payloads byte-equal the source stream; a fresh receiver consuming every frame reassembles the exact source bytes and the 25 decoded frames are identical; digest verifies
courts.incremental_playback: frame 0 available at the checkpoint; frames available per interval advance monotonically [1:2 2:3 ... 24:25], each prefix decoded through the normative parser equals the offline full-stream decode prefix (byte-exact canvas equality at every step)
courts.packet_loss: dropping one interval packet (seq 10) is a typed TransportGap and nothing applies; retransmission from seq 10 (20 frames) recovers the byte-exact stream; declaration-packet loss is also a typed gap
courts.checkpoint_recovery: receiver with 12 applied intervals rolls back to the checkpoint, replays the full 24-interval timeline from first_interval_seq, stream byte-identical; measured replay 24 intervals inside the 1,000,000-interval envelope bound
courts.corruption_hostile: payload byte flip inside an interval body -> typed feed error (non-consecutive interval, never a panic); integrity-digest byte flip -> verify()=false cleanly; truncated frame -> VoleError::Truncated; corrupted length word -> TransportFormat; unknown frame kind / header-not-first / interval-before-checkpoint / declaration-after-checkpoint / duplicate checkpoint / non-consecutive interval time / duplicate integrity / short integrity body / store-backed stream -> all typed (11 hostile forms in tests/phase_r.rs)
courts.missing_object: a checkpoint referencing an object whose OBJECT packet never arrived feeds cleanly but playback fails typed (UnknownObject) through the normative parser
courts.structural_innovation_33: deterministic 25-frame authored scenario (160x96): per-interval framed lane bytes track structural events - static 26 B, one absolute SetPosition 39 B, one palette-entry patch 37 B, one create_instance 43 B; 24-interval lane total 756 B < half of one 15,360-sample raster frame; the whole 25-frame transport is 1,488 framed B < one raster frame's samples; no residual anywhere (procedural state explains every frame exactly)
courts.amortized_unchanged_lane: same timeline + 200 static intervals (225 frames): measured 29 B/frame framed including the one-time object/palette/checkpoint declarations and 13 B/packet framing, vs 15,360 raster samples/frame - the unchanged lane's amortized cost is measured, never zeroed (§18)

test_count: tests/phase_r.rs (9 courts incl. hostile framing and the §33 measurement); full gate: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets (dev + all-features), cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings (0 warnings), cargo test (235), cargo test --all-features (237), cargo test --release --all-features (237) - 0 failures
notes: Transport is a framing/ordering layer, not a new normative format: every packet payload is a v1 record and the reassembled prefix + digest trailer is the standalone .vole stream (byte-exact for canonical sources, decode-identical always). No format-v1 constants changed; no old stream or golden was touched.

Single-checkpoint v1 files packetize with one checkpoint packet; multi-checkpoint cadence and OBJECT re-sync for long-running transport remain later-phase work (checkpoint cadence trade-offs §35 tracked when multi-checkpoint streams exist).
Store-backed (external-object) streams are rejected with a typed ApiConstraint - transporting them requires the store substrate (Phase P) and is a recorded boundary, not a silent fallback.

Synthetic small-canvas courts only: the §33 numbers demonstrate that on authored content the transported bytes respond to structural events and are minuscule fractions of the raster; no claim about natural video or a universal bandwidth law (§72).
Corruption courts confirm the §49 requirement for the transport domain: valid bounded decode or typed deterministic error - never panic, OOM, or hang.
